basis: Neurodevelopmental disorder; lymphatic vascular dysplasia and limb malformations are frequent per definition. Trafficking-related lymphopenia alone does not establish immunodeficiency.
Epithelial erosion confined to the uterine cervix; reproductive organs have no axis.
Intracranial arterial aneurysm; brain injury from rupture is a separately diagnosed complication, not intrinsic parenchymal involvement.
Benign serous adenofibroma of female reproductive organs, represented by ovarian and fallopian tube subtypes.
Defining skeletal dysplasia with mesomelic shortening. Renal, cardiac and dental abnormalities are occasional (5-29%); genital abnormalities have no axis.
Fungal or bacterial infection of subcutis; contiguous skeletal damage with abnormal bone structure and persistent foot deformity is frequent (30-79%).
Tubulointerstitial kidney disease; congenital anemia 5/5 and neutropenia 2/6 support blood involvement ([report](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27392076/)). Gout is separately coded.
Structural rupture of myocardium, cardiac septum, valves or associated supporting tissues.
Intellectual disability, congenital joint contractures and early retinal degeneration characterize this syndrome ([series](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5005468/)).
Germ cell tumor arising in the testis; reproductive tumor origin does not establish endocrine involvement.
Parasitic Demodex infestation involving cutaneous sebaceous glands.
Peripheral axonal neuropathy; persistent distal muscle denervation and atrophy are characteristic and common (>30%).
Mycobacterial infection defined by diffuse granulomatous skin lesions and symmetric peripheral nerve involvement.
Benign smooth muscle tumor arising in the uterine corpus; uterine muscle is outside the musculoskeletal axis.
Glycosylation defect with severe NDD; contractures 2/2, visual impairment 2/2 and optic atrophy 1/2. Respiratory insufficiency 1/2 lacks evidence of intrinsic lung damage.
Congenital lymphatic vascular malformation causing hydrops. Effusions and edema alone do not establish persistent pulmonary, cardiac or skin injury.
Drug or chemical toxicity directly injures the liver; an immune mechanism does not apply across this umbrella.
Polyposis is characteristic; callosal agenesis 3/3 supports direct CNS involvement. Cancer risks excluded ([guideline](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41431-024-01708-6)).
Pathologic TDP-43 inclusions directly damage brain and spinal cord neurons and glia; proteostasis ancestry alone does not establish a clinical metabolic disorder.
Respiratory motile cilia dysfunction with chronic airway disease. Otitis occurs in 1/11; situs inversus alone does not imply cardiovascular damage.
Breast carcinoma; breast has no axis, and receptor expression does not establish endocrine organ disease.
Destructive xanthogranulomatous inflammation of the gallbladder; infection or autoimmune disease is not established by this diagnosis.
Hereditary corticospinal tract disorder with spastic paraplegia and neurodevelopmental abnormalities; weakness and stiffness do not establish intrinsic muscle injury.
Defining limb synostoses and syndactyly; nail absence 11/12, renal agenesis 4/12 and hypoplasia 3/12. Dental loss 2/7 is borderline; other dental defects are <30%.
Peripheral motor-sensory neuropathy; persistent distal muscle atrophy in 20/20 and pes cavus in 3/7 support musculoskeletal involvement.
